question: Number of letters in the modern Bengali alphabet
funFact: Eleven vowels and thirty-nine consonants — the seventh most spoken script on earth.

question: Year the Kantajew Temple in Dinajpur was completed
funFact: Every inch of its outer wall is terracotta tile — an earthquake took its nine spires in 1897.

question: International dialling code for Bangladesh
funFact: Assigned in 1972 — India got 91 and Pakistan 92, so the region reads almost alphabetically.

question: Number of domes on the Shat Gambuj Mosque in Bagerhat
funFact: Its name means Sixty Dome Mosque, which it has never had — nobody agrees how the count got lost.

question: Number of monastic cells at the Somapura Mahavihara ruins in Paharpur
funFact: Built in the 8th century, it was the largest Buddhist monastery south of the Himalayas.

question: Year Emperor Akbar introduced the Bangla calendar (Bangabda)
funFact: It was a tax calendar — the harvest had to line up with when the collectors turned up.

question: Seats the Awami League won in East Pakistan in the 1970 general election
funFact: An outright majority of the whole Pakistani assembly, which was never allowed to sit.

question: Number of ethnic minority groups listed in Bangladesh's 2019 gazette
funFact: The Chakma are the largest; several on the list number only a few hundred people.

question: Number of tea gardens in Bangladesh
funFact: Most cluster around Sylhet and Moulvibazar, where the hills catch the monsoon.

question: Year the first tea garden was planted at Malnicherra in Sylhet
funFact: It is still producing, making it older than the Indian Rebellion by three years.

question: Year the first Bengali-language film from Dhaka, 'Mukh O Mukhosh', was released
funFact: The crew had no lab in Dhaka — the negatives went to Lahore to be developed.

question: Year BTV began broadcasting in colour
funFact: For most households the first colour thing on screen was a cricket match.

question: Runs Aminul Islam scored in Bangladesh's first ever Test innings in 2000
funFact: A century on debut for a whole country — only the third player in history to manage it.

question: Area of St Martin's Island in square kilometres
funFact: Bangladesh's only coral island, and you can walk from one end to the other before lunch.

question: Year Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal, splitting Dhaka from Kolkata
funFact: Dhaka got a capital out of it for six years, then lost it again when the split was reversed.

question: Year the rock band Miles was formed in Dhaka
funFact: They started out playing covers in hotel lobbies for tourists who wanted something familiar.

question: Number of Rabindra Sangeet songs Tagore is credited with writing
funFact: He wrote the national anthems of two countries and the tune of a third.

question: Year Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature
funFact: The first non-European to win it, for a book of poems he had translated himself.

question: Year Tagore wrote 'Amar Sonar Bangla', now the national anthem
funFact: It was a protest song against the partition of Bengal — only the first ten lines are sung.

question: Number of Nazrul Geeti songs Kazi Nazrul Islam is credited with
funFact: He lost his voice and memory to illness at 43 and never wrote again, living another 34 years.

question: Year Muhammad Yunus won the Nobel Peace Prize
funFact: Shared with Grameen Bank itself — the prize went to an institution and its founder together.

question: Year Musa Ibrahim became the first Bangladeshi to summit Everest
funFact: He carried the flag up and a national argument about the claim followed him back down.

question: Number of city corporations in Bangladesh
funFact: Dhaka counts as two of them — it was split into north and south in 2011.

question: Year Dhaka's city corporation was split into north and south
funFact: One city, two mayors, and an argument about which side owns the bits in the middle.

question: Number of players on each side in a kho kho match
funFact: Kabaddi is the national sport, but kho kho is the one every school field actually plays.

question: Year Jabbarer Boli Khela, Chattogram's wrestling festival, was first held
funFact: A trader started it to keep local men fighting fit against the British.

question: Diameter of the red disc on the Bangladesh flag, as a percent of the flag's length
funFact: Its radius is one fifth of the flag's length, and it sits left of centre so it looks centred when flying.

question: Year the Bangladesh national flag took its present form without the map
funFact: The 1971 version had a gold map of the country inside the red circle — impossible to draw twice the same.

question: Year Dhaka's first tram service was withdrawn from the streets
funFact: It ran for nearly half a century, then lost to buses in under a decade.

question: Year Bangladesh's first female Prime Minister took office
funFact: Khaleda Zia took office in 1991, and every PM since bar one caretaker has also been a woman.

question: Year Citycell switched on Bangladesh's first mobile phone network
funFact: A handset then cost more than a motorcycle, and incoming calls were billed too.

question: Year Grameenphone began operating in Bangladesh
funFact: Its village phone programme handed one handset per village to a woman who rented out calls.

question: Year Bangladesh connected to its first submarine internet cable, SEA-ME-WE 4
funFact: Bangladesh had turned down an earlier free connection in 1992 over security worries.

question: Year Bangladesh's garment export industry began with the Desh Garments deal
funFact: 130 workers trained in South Korea came home and seeded an industry worth billions.

question: Number of workers Desh Garments sent to South Korea for training in 1979
funFact: Almost all of them later left to start their own factories — the training escaped the company.

question: Sum the Dutch reportedly paid for Manhattan in 1626, in guilders
funFact: The only source is one sentence in one letter, and it never says who was paid.

question: What the USA paid for the Louisiana Purchase in 1803, in millions of dollars
funFact: About four cents an acre, for land that eventually became fifteen states.

question: What the USA paid Russia for Alaska in 1867, in millions of dollars
funFact: Mocked as Seward's Folly until gold turned up thirty years later.

question: Cost of building the Empire State Building in 1931, in millions of dollars
funFact: It came in under budget because the Depression had collapsed the price of labour.

question: What the Panama Canal had cost the USA by 1914, in millions of dollars
funFact: The French tried first, spent more, and gave up after losing over 20,000 workers.

question: Cost of building the Titanic, completed in 1912, in millions of dollars
funFact: Her sister ship Olympic sailed for 24 years without incident and nobody remembers her.

question: Final cost of the Sydney Opera House in 1973, in millions of Australian dollars
funFact: The original estimate was seven million, so it landed about fourteen times over budget.

question: Cost of the Channel Tunnel when it opened in 1994, in millions of pounds
funFact: Eighty percent over budget, and the operating company restructured its debt twice.

question: Cost of the Apollo programme through 1973, in billions of dollars
funFact: At its peak NASA was taking more than four percent of the entire federal budget.

question: Cost of the Manhattan Project by 1945, in millions of dollars
funFact: Most of it went on enriching uranium rather than on designing the bomb itself.

question: Cost of the James Webb Space Telescope by its 2021 launch, in millions of dollars
funFact: Budgeted at 500 million for a 2007 launch, so it arrived fourteen years and twentyfold late.

question: Cost of the Burj Khalifa when it opened in 2010, in millions of dollars
funFact: Dubai ran out of money mid-build and Abu Dhabi bailed it out, which is why the name changed.

question: Admission to Disneyland on its opening day in 1955, in cents
funFact: Rides were ticketed separately, and the E-ticket ones were the good ones.

question: What a three-day ticket to Woodstock cost in 1969, in dollars
funFact: So many turned up without one that the organisers gave up and declared it free.

question: Face value of a ticket to Super Bowl I in 1967, in dollars
funFact: The stadium still had 30,000 empty seats.

question: Cost of a 30-second advert during Super Bowl I in 1967, in dollars
funFact: Neither of the two networks that aired it kept a complete tape of the broadcast.

question: What a McDonald's hamburger cost in 1955, in cents
funFact: The whole menu had nine items, and fries were a dime.

question: What the first McDonald's Happy Meal cost in 1979, in cents
funFact: The original box was circus-themed and the toy was usually a stencil or an eraser.

question: Average US cinema admission in 1970, in cents
funFact: Adjusted for inflation that is close to today's — cinema pricing has barely moved in real terms.

question: Average US petrol pump price in 1970, in cents per gallon
funFact: The 1973 oil embargo roughly doubled it inside a year, and rationing followed.

question: US federal minimum wage in 1980, in cents per hour
funFact: It stayed frozen at 3.35 for the whole of the following nine years.

question: Average price of a new car in the USA in 1970, in dollars
funFact: That was roughly forty percent of the median household's entire annual income.

question: Median price of a US home in 1970, in thousands of dollars
funFact: The same house in the same street is now past four hundred thousand.

question: Postage on a US first-class letter in 1980, in cents
funFact: The Forever stamp arrived in 2007 precisely so nobody had to track this any more.

question: Peak price of an ounce of gold in January 1980, in dollars
funFact: It took twenty-eight years to reach that number again in nominal terms.

question: Dollar value of the two pizzas famously bought for 10,000 bitcoin in 2010
funFact: Bitcoin Pizza Day is marked every 22 May, mostly by people who did not do this.

question: What Salvator Mundi sold for at auction in 2017, in millions of dollars
funFact: Nobody has publicly seen it since, and experts still argue how much is really Leonardo.

question: Share price at which Amazon floated in 1997, in dollars
funFact: It sold books only, and the prospectus warned it might never turn a profit.

question: Price per share in Google's stock market debut in 2004, in dollars
funFact: They used a Dutch auction so ordinary buyers could get in, and Wall Street hated it.

question: Opening share price of the Facebook flotation in 2012, in dollars
funFact: It fell below that within days and took more than a year to climb back.

question: Share price at which Apple first went public in 1980, in dollars
funFact: It made roughly 300 people at the company millionaires in a single afternoon.

question: Sticker price of the Apple Lisa in 1983, in dollars
funFact: It flopped so badly that around 2,700 unsold units were buried in a Utah landfill.

question: What a Commodore 64 cost at its 1982 debut, in dollars
funFact: It is still the best-selling single computer model ever made.

question: What the Motorola DynaTAC 8000X mobile phone sold for in 1983, in dollars
funFact: Ten hours of charging bought you thirty minutes of talking.

question: What a Ford Model T cost in 1925, in dollars
funFact: It got cheaper almost every year of its life, which no car has managed since.

question: What a Sinclair ZX Spectrum 16K cost in Britain in 1982, in pounds
funFact: Its rubber keyboard felt like typing on a dead frog, a phrase reviewers used constantly.

question: What Sony's first Betamax television-recorder combo cost in 1975, in dollars
funFact: That bought the TV with the recorder inside it — you could not buy the deck alone.

question: Debut price of the Sony Discman D-50 CD player in 1984, in dollars
funFact: Sony priced it below cost on purpose, to get people buying compact discs at all.

question: What the Apple Newton MessagePad sold for in 1993, in dollars
funFact: Its handwriting recognition was mocked in Doonesbury and never recovered.

question: What a Palm Pilot 1000 sold for in 1996, in dollars
funFact: You had to learn its own alphabet, Graffiti, before you could write anything.

question: Debut price of the Segway in 2002, in dollars
funFact: It was hyped as bigger than the internet before anyone outside the company had seen it.

question: Base price of the first Tesla Roadster at its 2008 launch, in thousands of dollars
funFact: Only about 2,450 were built, and one of them is now orbiting the sun.

question: Monthly charge for America Online unlimited dial-up in 1996, in cents
funFact: The switch to unlimited jammed their network so badly that customers sued over busy signals.

question: Monthly charge for Netflix unlimited DVD-by-post in 2000, in cents
funFact: Blockbuster turned down the chance to buy the entire company for 50 million dollars.

question: Return airfare on Concorde from London to New York in 1997, in pounds
funFact: Surveys found passengers guessed a higher number, so British Airways raised it and sold more.

question: Temperature of a lightning bolt in degrees Celsius
funFact: Roughly five times the surface of the sun, which is why the air explodes into thunder.

question: Number of lightning strikes hitting the Earth every second
funFact: About 8 million a day, and roughly a quarter of them touch the ground.

question: Speed of sound through water in metres per second
funFact: Over four times its speed in air, which is why whale song carries for hundreds of kilometres.

question: Surface temperature of the Sun in degrees Celsius
funFact: The corona above it is 200 times hotter, and nobody fully agrees why.

question: Number of Earth days in a single day on Venus
funFact: Longer than its year — Venus goes round the sun faster than it turns once on its axis.

question: Height of Olympus Mons on Mars in kilometres
funFact: So wide and gentle that standing on it you could not tell you were on a mountain.

question: Length of the DNA in one human cell, uncoiled, in centimetres
funFact: Do it for every cell in your body and it reaches the sun and back dozens of times.

question: Number of separate muscles in a caterpillar's body
funFact: Humans manage about 600, and the caterpillar dissolves all of its own to become a moth.

question: Litres of blood the human heart pumps in a single day
funFact: Enough to fill a small swimming pool every fortnight.

question: Number of frets on a standard electric guitar neck
funFact: Twenty-four gives you exactly two octaves per string, which is why shredders insist on them.

question: Number of bones in the human foot
funFact: A quarter of all your bones are below your ankles.

question: Number of eyes a box jellyfish has
funFact: Some of them form proper images, despite the animal having no brain to look at them with.

question: Number of muscles in an elephant's trunk
funFact: It can lift a log or pick up a single grain of rice with the same appendage.

question: Number of quills on an adult porcupine
funFact: They cannot shoot them, whatever cartoons taught you — the quills simply detach on contact.

question: Number of wingbeats per second of a hummingbird in normal flight
funFact: Its heart runs at over 1,200 beats a minute to keep that up.

question: Number of times a woodpecker strikes a tree in a single day
funFact: Its skull takes around 1,200 g each time and it walks away with no concussion.

question: Depth in metres a sperm whale can dive when hunting squid
funFact: It holds its breath for around 90 minutes down there in total darkness.

question: Number of eyes a scallop can have around the rim of its shell
funFact: Each one has a mirror behind it instead of a lens, like a tiny telescope.

question: Number of chicken eggs equal in volume to one ostrich egg
funFact: It takes about 90 minutes to soft-boil, by which point it is nobody's idea of breakfast.

question: Number of legs on the leggiest millipede, found in Australia in 2021
funFact: The name millipede promises a thousand, and for two centuries none had ever delivered.

question: Number of days a camel can go without drinking water
funFact: The hump stores fat, not water — the trick is in the kidneys and the blood cells.

question: Number of panels stitched into a traditional football
funFact: Twenty hexagons and twelve pentagons — the same shape as a carbon-60 molecule.

question: Number of stitches on a regulation baseball
funFact: Every one is still sewn by hand, because no machine has matched the tension.

question: Number of ridges around the edge of a US quarter
funFact: Ridges began as anti-counterfeiting when coins were actually worth their metal.

question: Number of squares on a Scrabble board
funFact: The inventor worked out letter frequencies by counting them on the front page of a newspaper.

question: Number of letter tiles in a standard English Scrabble set
funFact: There are twelve Es and exactly one each of Q, Z, J, K and X.

question: Number of squares of every size that can be found on a chessboard
funFact: Sixty-four singles, plus every 2x2, 3x3 and so on up to the board itself.

question: Number of small cubes visible on the outside of a standard Rubik's Cube
funFact: The centre of the cube is not a cube at all, but the spindle that holds it together.

question: Number of strings on a standard concert harp
funFact: Seven pedals let one instrument play in every key without retuning a thing.

question: Scoville heat units of a typical jalapeno pepper
funFact: The scale began as a taste test — sugar water was added until the burn disappeared.

question: Scoville heat of the Carolina Reaper chilli, in thousands of units
funFact: Police-grade pepper spray sits in the same range, which tells you everything.

question: Number of grapes it takes to make one standard bottle of wine
funFact: Roughly one vine's entire annual output goes into two or three bottles.

question: Number of cocoa beans needed to make one kilogram of chocolate
funFact: One tree gives about a kilo of finished chocolate per year, after a decade of growing.

question: Number of seeds on the outside of an average strawberry
funFact: Botanically each seed is the actual fruit, and the red part is swollen stem tissue.

question: Number of times a sheet of paper has been folded in half, as a verified record
funFact: A schoolgirl did it in 2002 with 1,200 metres of toilet paper and a maths proof.

question: Number of Earths that would fit inside the Sun, in thousands
funFact: The Sun is still 99.86 percent of all the mass in the solar system.

question: Weight of an average cumulus cloud in tonnes
funFact: It floats because the air underneath it is denser, not because the cloud is light.

question: Number of bacteria species living in the average human mouth
funFact: Two people sharing a household still have mouths as different as their fingerprints.

question: Number of nerve endings in a single human fingertip
funFact: Fingertips can feel a bump 13 nanometres high — a molecule-scale defect on a smooth surface.

question: Number of litres of air an adult breathes in a day
funFact: About 22,000 breaths, and you consciously notice roughly none of them.

question: Number of scent receptor genes a dog has
funFact: Humans have about 400, which is more than most people assume.

question: Number of species of ants described by science
funFact: Their combined weight is estimated to rival that of all wild birds and mammals together.

question: Number of individual lenses in a dragonfly's compound eye
funFact: Nearly all of its brain is wired to vision, and it catches 95 percent of what it chases.

question: Distance in kilometres an Arctic tern migrates in a year
funFact: Over a lifetime that is roughly three return trips to the moon.

question: Number of teeth a great white shark grows through in its lifetime
funFact: They sit in rows on a conveyor, and a lost front tooth is replaced within days.

question: Number of small islands Venice is built on
funFact: Its buildings stand on millions of wooden piles driven into the mud, still holding after 1,500 years.

question: Number of stations on the London Underground
funFact: Only about 45 percent of the network is actually in a tunnel.

question: Number of steps from the ground to the top of the Eiffel Tower
funFact: The public can only walk as far as the second floor — the rest is a lift and a staff staircase.

question: Number of islands in the Indonesian archipelago
funFact: Only about 6,000 are inhabited, and thousands still have no official name.

question: Number of lakes in Finland
funFact: That is roughly one lake for every thirty people in the country.

question: Number of countries sharing a land border with Brazil
funFact: Only Chile and Ecuador escape it — Brazil touches every other country in South America.

question: Number of languages spoken in Papua New Guinea
funFact: More than a tenth of all the languages on earth, in a country of ten million people.

question: Number of tiles in a standard mahjong set
funFact: Sets often include spare blank tiles, because losing one ends the game permanently.

question: Number of ancient pyramids in Sudan
funFact: Sudan has roughly twice as many pyramids as Egypt, and a fraction of the visitors.

question: Number of times the International Space Station orbits Earth in a day
funFact: The crew sees sixteen sunrises a day and sleeps on a schedule that ignores all of them.

question: Speed of the International Space Station in kilometres per hour
funFact: At that speed you would cross Bangladesh in under a minute.

question: Number of years the Hundred Years' War actually lasted
funFact: It was also not one war but a run of separate ones, with decades of peace in between.

question: Number of terracotta warriors estimated to be buried at Xi'an
funFact: A farmer digging a well found them in 1974, and no two faces are alike.

question: Number of rooms in Buckingham Palace
funFact: Seventy-eight of them are bathrooms, which is a lot of plumbing for one address.

question: Number of steps inside the Statue of Liberty from the base to the crown
funFact: The crown has 25 windows and room for about a dozen people at a time.

question: Number of countries where traffic drives on the left
funFact: Mostly former British territories — Bangladesh, India and Japan all kept the habit.

question: Number of commercial flights in the air worldwide on a busy day
funFact: About 10,000 aircraft are airborne at any given moment during daylight peaks.

question: Length of the shortest war in history, the Anglo-Zanzibar War, in minutes
funFact: The losing side's palace was shelled before the ultimatum's ink was properly dry.

question: Character limit of a Twitter post before the 2017 change
funFact: It came from SMS, which allowed 160, leaving 20 characters for the username.

question: Number of Lego bricks that can be stacked before the bottom one is crushed
funFact: That tower would be over two and a half kilometres tall.

question: Length of the Trans-Siberian Railway in kilometres
funFact: Seven days end to end, crossing eight time zones without changing train.

question: Year the world's first website went live
funFact: It explained what the World Wide Web was, to an audience that had no way to find it.

question: Year Wikipedia was launched
funFact: It began as a throwaway side project to feed a slower, expert-written encyclopaedia.

question: Number of Academy Awards won by Titanic in 1998
funFact: It tied Ben-Hur's record, and Cameron quoted his own film accepting the last one.

question: Budget of the original Star Wars in 1977, in millions of dollars
funFact: Fox thought so little of it that they let Lucas keep the sequel and merchandising rights.

question: Number of takes Kubrick shot of one staircase scene in The Shining
funFact: It holds the record for most takes of a single scene with dialogue.

question: Number of stars on the flag of the European Union
funFact: The number has never changed with membership — twelve was chosen as a symbol of completeness.

question: Number of Academy Awards won by Walt Disney in his lifetime
funFact: He was nominated 59 times, which is still the record sixty years after his death.

question: Number of confirmed moons of Saturn as of 2023
funFact: It overtook Jupiter that year, after 62 new ones were confirmed at once.

question: Number of official languages recognised by the Indian constitution
funFact: Bengali is one of them, and is the second most spoken language in India.

question: Length of a marathon in metres
funFact: The odd 195 metres exists so the 1908 race could finish in front of the royal box.

question: Number of nations that competed at the 1896 Athens Olympics
funFact: Some competitors were tourists who happened to be in Athens and simply entered.

question: Year the Olympic marathon was first run over 42.195 kilometres
funFact: London stretched the course to finish in front of the royal box, and the odd number stuck.

question: Height of a men's volleyball net in centimetres
funFact: The women's net is 224, and both numbers come from a 1947 committee that never explained them.

question: Weight of a men's cricket ball in grams
funFact: The permitted range is only about eight grams wide, and umpires carry scales.

question: Points Wilt Chamberlain scored in a single NBA game in 1962
funFact: No photographs of the game exist and no broadcast survives — 4,124 people saw it.

question: Year the first Formula One World Championship season was run
funFact: The opening race was at Silverstone, on a circuit made from a wartime bomber airfield.

question: Number of laps in the Indianapolis 500
funFact: The winner drinks milk, a tradition started by a driver who simply fancied buttermilk.

question: Balls in an over in Australian domestic cricket until 1979
funFact: England, Australia and South Africa all experimented before six became universal.

question: Runs Brian Lara scored in his unbeaten Test innings in 2004
funFact: He had already held the record, lost it, and took it back within six months.

question: Runs Mushfiqur Rahim scored in his double century against Zimbabwe in 2018
funFact: The first Bangladeshi to score two Test double hundreds, and he kept wicket as well.

question: Balls Shahid Afridi took to reach his ODI century in 1996
funFact: He was seventeen, batting with a bat borrowed from Sachin Tendulkar.

question: Year the Miracle on Ice ice hockey upset took place
funFact: American college students beat a Soviet side that had won every Olympic gold since 1964.

question: Year Bangladesh first reached a Cricket World Cup quarter-final
funFact: Mahmudullah scored back-to-back hundreds, the first Bangladeshi ever to do it at a World Cup.

question: Year Bangladesh beat Australia in the Cardiff ODI upset
funFact: Mohammad Ashraful's hundred beat the world champions, who had lost twice in two years.

question: Year Roger Bannister ran the first sub-four-minute mile
funFact: His record lasted 46 days, and over 1,700 people have since done it.

question: Usain Bolt's 100 metres world record from 2009, in hundredths of a second
funFact: He was still slowing down and celebrating in the last ten metres of the 2008 version.

question: Number of gold medals Michael Phelps won at the 2008 Beijing Olympics
funFact: One of them was decided by a hundredth of a second, on a fingertip.

question: Year the first Tour de France was held
funFact: A newspaper invented it to sell copies, and it worked — circulation went up sixfold.

question: Year Sachin Tendulkar scored the first double century in ODI cricket
funFact: Thirty-nine years and 2,962 matches had passed without anyone managing it.

question: Number of bones in a single hilsa fish
funFact: Which is why eating one properly counts as a skill rather than a meal.

question: Threads per inch in the finest historic Dhaka muslin
funFact: The best cotton made anywhere today manages about 500, and the technique was lost for a century.

question: Years Bangladesh waited between its first ODI and its first ODI win
funFact: Twenty-two matches of losing, from 1986 to 1998, and then they beat Kenya.

question: Mobile SIM connections per 100 people in Bangladesh in 2024
funFact: More SIMs than people — the second one is for whichever network works at your nani's house.

question: Number of books Humayun Ahmed published in his lifetime
funFact: Roughly a book every two months for thirty years, and he directed films on the side.

question: Number of government public holidays in Bangladesh in 2024
funFact: Among the most generous counts in the world, and still nobody thinks it is enough.

question: Number of bird species recorded in Bangladesh
funFact: In a country the size of England and Wales, half of which is underwater by August.

question: Number of passengers a single Dhaka Metro Rail train is built to carry
funFact: Only 306 of those get a seat, which explains the sprint when the doors open.

question: Years the Dhaka Metro spent under construction before its first passenger
funFact: Ground broken in 2012, first ticket sold in 2022, and the traffic below is unchanged.

question: Age Mohammad Ashraful was when he scored a century on Test debut
funFact: Still the youngest player ever to score a Test hundred, and he did it against Sri Lanka.

question: Number of floors in City Centre Dhaka, the country's tallest building
funFact: Dhaka has twenty million people and its tallest building would be unremarkable in Chicago.

question: Number of hours a cockroach can survive without its head
funFact: It breathes through its body and dies of thirst, not of the missing head.

question: Number of hours Randy Gardner stayed awake in his 1964 record attempt
funFact: Eleven days. By the end he could not say the alphabet, and Guinness later retired the category.

question: Litres of methane a single cow belches out in a day
funFact: It comes out of the front end, not the back, which ruins the joke everyone makes.

question: Number of hours a sloth takes to digest one leaf
funFact: A month per leaf, and it climbs all the way down to the ground once a week to relieve itself.

question: Number of bacteria on a typical phone screen, per square centimetre
funFact: Comfortably more than the average toilet seat, and you hold it against your face.

question: Decibels of the loudest burp ever recorded
funFact: Louder than a chainsaw, and the record holder trained for it deliberately.

question: Number of hot dogs eaten in ten minutes to set the 2021 Nathan's record
funFact: Buns included. The winner has held the title for most of two decades.

question: Number of moves in the longest competitive chess game ever played
funFact: It took over twenty hours in 1989 and ended, inevitably, in a draw.

question: Number of years Charles Osborne hiccupped without stopping
funFact: They started in 1922 and stopped on their own in 1990. He died the following year.

question: Number of times lightning struck park ranger Roy Sullivan
funFact: He survived every one of them, and his hat caught fire more than once.

question: Number of eggs a single housefly lays in its lifetime
funFact: It manages this inside about four weeks, which is the entire life of a housefly.

question: Number of drops that have fallen in the Pitch Drop Experiment since 1927
funFact: Nobody witnessed the first eight. The professor who watched it for decades died in 1979.

question: Number of Big Macs Don Gorske had eaten by 2023
funFact: He kept every receipt, and his cholesterol is reportedly fine.

question: Number of hours the longest recorded game of Monopoly lasted
funFact: Seventy days. The game was designed to teach people that landlords are bad.

question: Olympic Games Bangladesh has competed in without winning a medal, through 2024
funFact: The largest country in the world never to have won one, which is a record of a kind.

question: Number of stripes on a Royal Bengal Tiger
funFact: No two tigers share a pattern, and the stripes are on the skin as well as the fur.

question: Number of islands making up the Sundarbans
funFact: Fifty-four of them have no people on them at all, which is how the tigers prefer it.

question: Number of digits in a Bangladeshi mobile phone number
funFact: Everyone can recite their own and nobody can recite anyone else's any more.

question: Number of lines in Tagore's full 'Amar Sonar Bangla' poem
funFact: Only the first ten are the national anthem, so most Bangladeshis have never heard the ending.

question: Year Dhaka's rickshaw art joined UNESCO's intangible heritage list
funFact: A century of painting film stars and tigers onto the back of a bicycle, formally recognised.

question: Road distance from Dhaka to Cox's Bazar in kilometres
funFact: Ten hours by bus, or forty minutes by air, and everyone still argues about which is better.

question: Number of kilograms in one Bangladeshi mon
funFact: Rice, jute and mangoes are all still sold by the mon, and nobody under thirty can convert it.

question: Number of seasons in the traditional Bengali calendar
funFact: Six, against everyone else's four — including one entire season for the monsoon.

question: Number of years Dhaka's tram service ran before it was scrapped
funFact: Opened under the British in 1889 and beaten by buses by the early fifties.

question: Number of vocal sounds a cat can make, against a dog's ten
funFact: Adult cats essentially only meow at humans. Between themselves they do not bother.

question: Number of toes on a normal cat
funFact: Five in front, four behind. Hemingway's cats had extras and the house is still full of them.

question: Number of whiskers on a typical cat
funFact: Twelve a side, and they are roughly as wide as the cat — a built-in width gauge.

question: Number of bones in a cat's body
funFact: About thirty more than a human, and a good number of them are in the tail.

question: Number of colour receptors in a mantis shrimp's eye
funFact: Humans have three. Testing suggests it is somehow worse at telling colours apart than we are.

question: Number of teeth on a garden snail's tongue
funFact: Arranged in rows on a ribbon it scrapes food with, and it grows replacements constantly.

question: Number of Bangladeshi districts that share a land border with India
funFact: Thirty of the sixty-four. The border runs for over four thousand kilometres.

question: Number of union parishads, the lowest tier of local government in Bangladesh
funFact: Every one of them elects a chairman, which is a great many elections.

question: Number of minutes a giraffe sleeps in a 24-hour day
funFact: Taken in five-minute naps, mostly standing up, because lying down is a commitment.

question: Litres of water an adult elephant drinks in a day
funFact: It can smell water from several kilometres away and dig for it when there is none.

question: Weight of a newborn giant panda in grams
funFact: About the size of a stick of butter, born to a mother nine hundred times heavier.

question: Number of hours a giant panda spends eating each day
funFact: Bamboo is so poor in nutrition that a panda's schedule has no room for anything else.

question: Number of wingbeats per second of a mosquito
funFact: That whine in the dark is the wingbeat, and it is how they find each other to mate.

question: Number of flowers a honeybee colony visits to make one teaspoon of honey
funFact: One bee makes about a twelfth of a teaspoon in its entire working life.

question: Number of minutes the average person spends dreaming each night
funFact: Two hours a night, and you will forget almost all of it within five minutes of waking.

question: Number of decisions the average person makes about food each day
funFact: A Cornell study found people guessed about fifteen, then were shown the tally.

question: Number of words the average person speaks in a day
funFact: Men and women came out within a few hundred of each other, ending a long argument.

question: Number of licks it took a machine to reach a Tootsie Pop's centre
funFact: Students have been re-running this experiment since 1970 and no two get the same number.

question: Number of ways to make change for one US dollar
funFact: A standard puzzle for teaching recursion, and the answer surprises nearly everyone.

question: Number of times the human body rebuilds its entire skeleton in a lifetime
funFact: Roughly one full replacement per decade, bone by bone, without telling you.

question: Number of litres of saliva a person produces in a lifetime
funFact: Enough to fill two swimming pools, which is not a thought anyone needed.

question: Number of muscles in the human tongue
funFact: It is not the strongest muscle in the body either, whatever you were told at school.

question: Number of times a dog's sense of smell beats a human's
funFact: It can also smell in stereo, using each nostril separately to work out direction.

question: Minute Zinedine Zidane was sent off in the 2006 World Cup final
funFact: His last act as a professional footballer was a headbutt to the chest, on live television.

question: Goals Australia scored against American Samoa in their 2001 World Cup qualifier
funFact: American Samoa's goalkeeper was fifteen, and most of the squad had never played together.

question: Length of the Isner-Mahut Wimbledon match in minutes, in 2010
funFact: Eleven hours over three days. The scoreboard broke because it could not display the score.

question: Number of aces John Isner served in that 2010 Wimbledon marathon
funFact: More aces than most players hit in a whole tournament, and he lost in the next round.

question: US launch price of the Apple I in 1976, in dollars
funFact: Wozniak picked 666.66 because he liked repeating digits, then spent years explaining it.

question: What the first item ever sold on eBay went for in 1995, in cents
funFact: A broken laser pointer. The seller checked the buyer knew it was broken. He did — he collected them.

question: What Yahoo offered to buy Google for in 2002, in millions of dollars
funFact: Google wanted five billion, Yahoo walked away, and the price was later somewhat higher.

question: What the Wright brothers spent building the 1903 Flyer, in dollars
funFact: Funded out of a bicycle shop, while a government-backed rival spent fifty times as much and crashed.

question: Price per kilogram of kopi luwak coffee in 2024, in dollars
funFact: The beans are eaten and passed by a civet first. People pay a premium for this.

question: Number of years the Eiffel Tower was originally meant to stand
funFact: It was saved by being useful as a radio mast, not by anyone deciding they liked it.

question: Number of bags of human waste left behind on the Moon
funFact: Mass had to be saved for the rocks coming back, so something else had to stay.

question: Number of people who have been to space, through 2024
funFact: Fewer than fill a decent-sized cinema, and a growing share of them bought a ticket.

question: Number of trackable pieces of space junk orbiting Earth in 2024
funFact: Anything above ten centimetres. Below that there are tens of millions nobody can see.

question: Number of stars visible to the naked eye from Earth on a clear night
funFact: Across the whole sky and both hemispheres — from one spot you get about half.

question: Number of emoji in the Unicode standard as of 2024
funFact: A committee meets to approve each one, and rejected proposals include a rock.

question: Number of letters in the Hawaiian alphabet
funFact: Missionaries pared it down in 1826 and threw away half the consonants.

question: Number of official languages of the European Union
funFact: Every document gets translated into all of them, which employs several thousand people.

question: Number of time zones France spans, counting its overseas territories
funFact: More than any other country, Russia included, thanks to islands in three oceans.

question: Number of countries Britain has invaded at some point in history
funFact: Out of roughly 193. The short list of ones it missed includes Luxembourg and Bolivia.

question: Number of letters in the longest word in a major English dictionary
funFact: A lung disease named in 1935 by a puzzle enthusiast specifically to be the longest word.

question: Number of works of art Vincent van Gogh produced in his lifetime
funFact: Most of them in his last two years, and he reliably sold almost none of them.

question: Seconds the average visitor spends looking at the Mona Lisa
funFact: Most of that through a phone screen held above the head of the person in front.

question: Number of steps from the bottom to the top of the Empire State Building
funFact: There is an annual race up them. The record is under ten minutes.

question: Number of windows in the Empire State Building
funFact: A full clean takes months, at which point it is time to start again.

question: Number of floors in the Burj Khalifa
funFact: The top thirty or so are unoccupied spire — the useful building stops well below the summit.

question: Centimetres the Eiffel Tower grows on a hot summer day
funFact: The iron expands, and it also leans slightly away from the sun as one side warms.

question: Number of years it took to finish building the Leaning Tower of Pisa
funFact: It started leaning after five, and the long pauses for war are why it never fell over.

question: Number of words in the original US Constitution, excluding amendments
funFact: One of the shortest national constitutions in the world, and the oldest still in use.

question: Number of languages Google Translate supported in 2024
funFact: It added 110 in a single 2024 update, including several with under a million speakers.

question: Number of pieces in a standard chess set
funFact: The queen was the weakest piece for centuries before becoming the strongest around 1500.

question: Number of chambers in a cockroach's heart
funFact: It can keep pumping with several of them out of action, which is part of the problem.

question: Number of suckers on a single octopus arm
funFact: Each one can taste what it touches, so an octopus tastes everything it picks up.

question: Number of feathers on an adult chicken
funFact: Someone counted. Several someones, in fact, and they broadly agree.

question: Number of eggs a good laying hen produces in a year
funFact: Wild jungle fowl, the same species, manage about twelve.

question: Number of times a chicken's heart beats per minute
funFact: A blue whale's manages about eight, and both animals get roughly the same lifetime total.

question: Number of bones in a swan's neck
funFact: A giraffe has seven, the same as you — length comes from bigger bones, not more of them.

question: Number of teeth in a dolphin's mouth
funFact: It never chews with any of them — everything is swallowed whole and head-first.

question: Number of minutes a newborn foal takes to stand up
funFact: Prey animals get no childhood. A human takes about a year to manage the same trick.

question: Number of species of octopus known to science
funFact: One of them, the mimic octopus, impersonates at least fifteen other animals.

question: Number of eggs an ocean sunfish can release at once, in millions
funFact: More than any other vertebrate, and almost none of them survive to adulthood.

question: Litres of slime a hagfish can produce in under a minute
funFact: It has to sneeze to clear its own airway afterwards, having nearly suffocated itself.

question: Number of times its own body length a flea can jump
funFact: It uses a stored spring of elastic protein — muscle alone could not do it.

question: Number of days a scorpion can survive without eating
funFact: It can also slow its metabolism to a third of the normal rate and simply wait.

question: Number of frames per second a housefly can perceive
funFact: You move in slow motion to a fly, which is exactly why the newspaper never lands.

question: Number of days a red blood cell survives before being replaced
funFact: It has no nucleus and cannot repair itself, so the body simply builds new ones constantly.

question: Number of different smells a human nose can distinguish, in millions
funFact: The old textbook figure was 10,000, which turned out to be a guess from 1927.

question: Number of bacteria living on one square centimetre of human skin
funFact: Your forearm hosts more species than a rainforest patch of the same size.

question: Number of hairs in a human eyebrow
funFact: Each one lives about four months, which is why a bad eyebrow decision is survivable.
